charged_prices.direction: charged = measured compiled body >= executed (v34 charged below measured)

address_correspondence: signed 64-bit/limb model, as in v34: one instruction per address and one per operand access. Static counts are unsigned bodies; the multiplier-up expansions are declared in derive, not hidden. This is a model, and the model is what the claim is expressed in.

pool_level.definition: long-walk rungs, ell >= 64, plus the primary re-run
pool_level.level: pool level: production consumes ONE pool (nb bases x one shared walk list), so the Cartesian record set IS the trial unit; the floor is asserted here and reported per rung below

rungs_below_floor.disclosure: the two counts differ because the ell=16 and ell=1 controls are outside the claim population. The claim does NOT rest on 'all rungs clear': it rests on the pooled endpoint with the rung spread disclosed and Q non-significant.

heterogeneity.driver: ell=16 short-walk control is out of the claim population and is the entire driver of the all-seven statistic

cluster_bootstrap_over_rungs.note: THE ONLY bootstrap interval in this package; no other interval is quoted anywhere

success.reconciliation: ONE bootstrap interval in the whole package, the one computed by ladder_v35.py; the v34 text's [0.3922,0.3972] is withdrawn. Rung count: 2 of the 5 long-walk rungs are below 0.39 (the third, ell=16, is outside the claim population).
success.transfer_statement: the claim is a POOL-level statement about the trial unit production consumes (one pool = Cartesian base x walk). The fixture's absolute nb/ell split is NOT claimed transferable; the structure is.

kappa.rule: max per-pool p95 over POWERED cells (birthday-expected pairs >= 100), floored at the carried 1.231 envelope; every cell measures its own pair rate against its own birthday prediction, so this is a collision law and not a hash-bit artefact
kappa.census_object: e -> [e mod r]G -> x-coordinate, masked to b bits

trend.extrapolation: the largest POWERED width is 24 bits; the 168-bit production envelope is charged at the measured p95 with the carried floor, NOT by extrapolating a bit-dependence slope. The 24->168 step is a declared hypothesis.
trend.why_not_slope: a per-bit dependence fit is not evidence about a 168-bit coordinate; the charge is max(measured p95, 1.231) and the residual step is disclosed

kappa.fixture_disclosure: 31-bit-prime curve, real prime-order subgroup found by BSGS, keys are real x-coordinates: the collision law is measured on the production MAP with a small SPACE. No SHAKE, no synthetic modulus. Transfer of the absolute kappa to 381-bit coordinates is NOT claimed; the pairwise law and its upper envelope are.

gap_support.markov_fallback: P(gap>t) <= E[gap]/t with NO tail assumption: a Markov-on-observed-max row. It is insufficient on its own (2^-6.9 per gap), so it is stated as a failure and the charge does not depend on the geometric hypothesis: the gap row is 2^93.873 of 2^116.854 total, moving the claim < 1e-4 bits.
gap_support.geometric_tail: HYPOTHESIS, retained only as a sensitivity: not the basis of the claim

executed_counts.note: same compiled body, two input sizes: 372 vs 21 executed inner steps. The static count (257) is a constant; the dynamic cost is not. Every row is therefore charged at max(static, executed) and the sort row carries the executed count for n=25.

fixes.op_fp381_inv: new anchor: the inversion the chain-table entry is priced with; static 45, transitive 569.
fixes.op_fp381_mulmod: v34 multiplied 6x6 limbs and truncated: P381 was never referenced, so the anchor was not a mulmod. v35 keeps the 6x6 product and adds a real reduction mod P381 by binary shift-subtract over the 12-limb product plus a final conditional subtract. Static instructions 90 -> 262 (+172). The price RISES; the anchor now contains the operation it is named for.
fixes.op_point_construct: v34 did three multiplications and eight squarings: no point addition, no inversion. v35 computes lambda=(y2-y1)/(x1-x2) with a Fermat chain inv(z)=z^(p-2), then x3=lam^2-x1-x2 and y3=lam(x1-x3)-y1. Static 104, transitive 1617 instructions.

anchors.chain: source -> clang -O2 -> otool -tV -> instructions -> price -> row (all in-tree)
